_doc: High or critical advisories the audit floor gate (check-audit-floor.mjs) accepts on purpose, keyed by package directory (the keys are also the only directories the script runs from). Fields: `ghsa` the advisory id as `npm audit` reports it (the GHSA id, or `npm-<source id>` for an advisory without a GitHub URL; the gate's FAIL line names it); `package` the vulnerable package (an entry matches on ghsa AND package); `range` the vulnerable range and `severity` the severity as `npm audit` reported them when the entry was reviewed (ranges compare as semver sets, so re-formatting is not a change; when npm audit reports a different range or severity the advisory has moved, usually because a patch was published, and the gate FAILs until a human re-reviews the entry; it also FAILs an entry when npm reports a reachable fix, `fixAvailable` true or a non-major parent change); `why` the reasoning (why no override can fix it); `revisit` the condition that retires the entry. A matching advisory prints as `accepted` and does not fail the gate; an entry the audit no longer reports, or now reports below high, prints as `stale`, for a human to remove in a reviewed PR. A repeated (ghsa, package) pair stops the gate (exit 2). The scan never edits this file. Tests point the script at their own copy through ACCEPTED_ADVISORIES_FILE. Reasoning: docs/automation/daily-upgrade-scan.md, 'Audit floor gate'.

mobile.why: Quadratic-time replacement of percent-encoded runs: a crafted string makes decoding slow. The only copy is decode-uri-component 0.2.2 under expo-router 57 -> query-string 7.1.3 (^0.2.2), which parses URLs on the user's own device, so the worst case is a slow parse of a link that user opened, never a server or another user. The only patched release, 0.5.1, is ESM-only and breaks query-string under Jest (Unexpected token 'export'), and a version-keyed override desyncs npm ci (#275). npm's only fix is expo-router 58 (Expo SDK 58), which needs a new native binary (#922). Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-06.
mobile.revisit: With the Expo SDK 58 binary (#922), whose expo-router no longer pulls decode-uri-component (Dependabot #997), or a CommonJS patched release: take it and remove this entry in the same PR.
